cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is still preaching to Israel, and friend, this man has NOT run out of things to say. Now he looks ahead to the day the LORD has cut off the nations whose land He's giving Israel. Israel will drive them out and settle into their cities and houses.

cards.question: Once Israel settles in, Moses tells them to set apart ___ cities in the land.

cards.text: THREE, and he wants roads built and the whole land divided into three regions. Moses is preaching a sermon and planning a whole road map in the same breath. I can't even stamp a cookie and talk at the same time!

cards.question: Why does Moses want roads built and the land divided into three regions around these three cities?

answers.text: So any manslayer can flee to them
So the Levites can collect offerings
So the tribes can trade their goods

cards.text: Then Moses gets specific. He describes the kind of manslayer he has in mind: one who runs to one of these cities to save his life.

cards.question: What kind of manslayer does Moses describe fleeing to one of these cities to save his life?

answers.text: One who killed his neighbor by accident
One who killed his neighbor in a quarrel
One who killed his neighbor for revenge

cards.text: By accident, without meaning him any harm. Picture two neighbors heading into the forest to cut timber, and one of them swings his axe at a tree.

cards.question: In Moses' example, what goes wrong when the man swings his axe at the tree?

answers.text: The blade flies off the handle
The tree falls the wrong way

cards.text: The blade hits his neighbor and kills him. Moses says this man may flee to one of these cities to save his life.

cards.question: Why does the man whose axe blade flew off need to flee to one of these cities?

answers.text: The avenger of blood might chase him down
The elders might sell him as a servant
The priests might bar him from worship

cards.question: True or false: Moses says the man whose axe blade flew off deserves to die for what happened.

cards.text: If the city's too far, the avenger could chase him in a rage and catch him, though he didn't deserve to die. A refuge city that far away is like a fire exit at the end of a forty-minute hallway!
That's why Moses commands three cities. Then he looks further down the road: what if the LORD enlarges their territory, as He swore to their fathers, and gives them all the land He promised?

cards.question: If the LORD gives Israel all the land He promised, Moses says to add ___ more cities to the first three.
True or false: Moses says the extra cities depend on Israel carefully keeping the commandments, loving the LORD and walking in His ways.
Moses says the cities of refuge are there so that ___ blood will not be shed in the land.

cards.text: Now Moses flips the whole thing around. What if a man hates his neighbor, lies in wait, attacks him, kills him, and THEN runs to one of these cities?

cards.question: When a man who killed his neighbor on purpose runs to a city of refuge, what must the elders of his own city do?

answers.text: Bring him back to the avenger of blood
Let him live in the refuge city
Send him to stand before the priests

cards.question: True or false: Moses tells Israel to show some pity to the man who killed his neighbor on purpose.

cards.text: No pity: Israel must purge the guilt of shedding innocent blood, so it may go well with them. Those cities are for accidents, friend, not a game of tag where you touch the gate and yell SAFE!
Then Moses switches to land. He talks about the boundary markers their ancestors set up to mark the inheritance in the land the LORD is giving them.

cards.question: Moses says Israel must not ___ a neighbor's boundary marker.

cards.text: Next up, the courtroom. Moses says one lone witness isn't enough to prove a man did wrong, no matter what the offense is.

cards.question: If one witness isn't enough, how many witnesses does it take to establish a matter?

cards.text: Two or three, friend. If one was enough, the mystery key I shared that junk drawer with could've accused me of ANYTHING. That key couldn't even figure out which door it opened!
But what if a witness lies and accuses someone of a crime? Moses says the dispute goes before the LORD.

cards.question: True or false: in a case with a false witness, only the accused person has to stand before the priests and judges.
In a case with a false witness, what must the judges do?

cards.text: And say the judges prove the witness is a liar who falsely accused his brother. Oh, that story just fell apart like a cookie pulled out two minutes early!

cards.question: What does Moses say Israel must do to the witness who lied about his brother?

answers.text: Do to him what he intended for his brother
Make him pay a fine to the priests
Send him away to a city of refuge

cards.question: Moses says that when the rest of the people hear what happened to the lying witness, they will be ___.

cards.text: Then Moses sums it up: "You must show no pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, and foot for foot."

cards.question: True or false: with "eye for eye, tooth for tooth," Moses means the penalty should match the harm.

cards.text: And that's where we'll pause, friend. Moses is nowhere near done with this sermon, so keep that apron on.

findings.problem: This story card is not the opening card, but it has 3 sentences: "THREE, and he wants roads built…", "Moses is preaching a sermon…" and "I can't even stamp a cookie…". Trim it to 1 or 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke is built on a game of tag ("touch the gate and yell SAFE"). Tag is a children's game, and the audience rule bans scenarios aimed at kids. Replace it with an adult comparison that has the same core action: running to a safe place to escape the consequences.

rule.text: No jokes or scenarios about school, parents or anything aimed at kids. Work, bosses and bills are fine.

findings.problem: This card tells no new part of the passage. Card 8 already answered "Two or three" from 19:15, and card 7 already covered the lone witness. Card 9 repeats that answer and adds a joke, so it works as a recap. Remove it, or move the joke onto a card that carries a new moment.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The punchline makes the mystery key the butt of the joke ("That key couldn't even figure out which door it opened!"). It also pictures a drawer friend falsely accusing him. Papa Dorin's humor should land on himself, not on the friends he looked after.

rule.text: Humble. When a joke needs someone to laugh at, it's himself.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences. Trim it to 1 or 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The statement marked True says the penalty should "match the harm." In this passage, 19:19 ties the penalty to what the false witness intended to do to his brother, and his lie may have caused no harm at all. That makes the statement imprecise. A baker who reasons from 19:19 could fairly argue it is false. Reword it to match the text, for example "the liar gets what he intended for his brother," and cite 19:19, 21.

rule.text: He never says anything the text shows is wrong.
